proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\), and write \(\mathcal L=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\). The conditional moments below exist by \(\texttt{ass:moment-radius}\), and conditioning on cohort \(c\) is legitimate because \(p_c\geq p_{\star}>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:positive-shares}\). By \(\texttt{ass:rank-two-factor-law}\) and \(\texttt{ass:error-mean}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\nu_c
&=\mathbb E_P[J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c]\\
&=\mathbb E_P[\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c]\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
Similarly, \(\texttt{ass:loading-error-orthogonality}\) makes both cross-covariance terms vanish, and \(\texttt{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
V_c
&=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c)\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}
  +\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c)\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\), the positive-semidefinite first summand in (2) has rank two and its second eigenvalue is at least \(g_{\star}>0\). Consequently the two largest eigenvalues of \(V_c\) strictly exceed \(\sigma_c^2\), while its remaining \(|S_c|-2\) eigenvalues equal \(\sigma_c^2\). Therefore
\[
\Pi_2(V_c)=\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})},
\qquad
Q_c=I_{|S_c|}-\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})}.
\tag{3}
\]
The entire observed law \(P_O\) determines \(p_c\), \(\nu_c\), and \(V_c\) for every \(c\), since \(p_c>0\). Thus it determines every local plane in (3).

Choose \(B_c\) as in \(\texttt{def:relation-operator}\). Since \(B_c^{\prime}B_c=Q_c\),
\[
\|B_cy\|^2=y^{\prime}Q_cy
\qquad (y\in\mathbb R^{|S_c|}),
\]
and hence \(\ker B_c=\ker Q_c=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\). Positivity of every \(p_c\) now yields the basis-independent identity
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal K(P):=\ker\overline R(P)
&=\bigcap_{c=1}^C\ker(B_cJ_c)\\
&=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^T:x_{S_c}\in
\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\text{ for every }c\in[C]\right\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
In particular, \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal K(P)\), and (4) shows that \(\mathcal K(P)\), despite the nonuniqueness of the row bases \(B_c\), is a functional of \(P_O\).

By \(\texttt{lem:generic-rank-two-coordinate-projection-certificate}\), applied under \(\texttt{ass:fixed-dimensions}\), \(\texttt{ass:deterministic-masks}\), and \(\texttt{ass:generic-factor-rows}\), the local planes \(\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\) determine \(\mathcal L\) uniquely if and only if the anchor multihypergraph from \(\texttt{def:anchor-hypergraph}\) contains a set \(F\) of \(T-2\) triples satisfying
\[
|F'|\leq |V(F')|-2
\qquad\text{for every nonempty }F'\subseteq F.
\tag{5}
\]
By \(\texttt{def:pebble-certificate}\), this is equivalent to \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). Such an \(F\) automatically spans \([T]\), because (5) with \(F'=F\) implies
\[
T-2=|F|\leq |V(F)|-2\leq T-2,
\]
so \(|V(F)|=T\).

We next show that uniqueness of the global plane is equivalent to \(\mathcal K(P)=\mathcal L\). If \(\mathcal K(P)=\mathcal L\) and a two-dimensional subspace \(\widetilde{\mathcal L}\) has \((\widetilde{\mathcal L})_{S_c}=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\) for all \(c\), then (4) gives \(\widetilde{\mathcal L}\subseteq\mathcal K(P)=\mathcal L\); equality follows because both spaces have dimension two. Conversely, suppose that \(\mathcal K(P)\supsetneq\mathcal L\). Choose \(h\in\mathcal K(P)\setminus\mathcal L\) and a basis \(u_1,u_2\) of \(\mathcal L\). For \(z\neq0\), put
\[
\mathcal L_z=\operatorname{span}(u_1+zh,u_2).
\tag{6}
\]
The two displayed generators are linearly independent: otherwise, because \(z\neq0\), one could solve for \(h\in\mathcal L\). Hence \(\dim(\mathcal L_z)=2\), and \(\mathcal L_z\neq\mathcal L\) for the same reason. Equation (4) gives \((\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}\subseteq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\). At \(z=0\), the restricted pair has rank two for each \(c\), because \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\) implies \(\operatorname{rank}(\Gamma_{S_c})=2\). For every cohort, select a nonzero two-by-two minor of the restricted pair at \(z=0\). Each selected minor is continuous in \(z\), and \(C<\infty\) by \(\texttt{ass:fixed-dimensions}\); therefore all selected minors remain nonzero for every sufficiently small \(|z|>0\). For such a \(z\),
\[
(\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})
\qquad\text{for every }c\in[C].
\tag{7}
\]
Thus strict inclusion in (4) produces a distinct compatible two-dimensional plane. We have proved
\[
r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal K(P)=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma).
\tag{8}
\]
In particular, certificate failure implies \(\ker\overline R(P)=\mathcal K(P)\supsetneq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\), and (6)--(7) supply the asserted plane \(\widetilde{\mathcal L}\).

Suppose now that \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). Let \(U\) be any orthonormal basis of the observed-law kernel \(\mathcal K(P)\). By (8) and \(\texttt{ass:factor-normalization}\), there is an orthogonal \(W\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\) with \(U=\Gamma W\). The local signal gap implies that \(\Gamma_{S_c}\), and hence \(U_{S_c}\), has full column rank. Thus \(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c}\) is positive definite. Set \(G_c=\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}\Gamma_{S_c}\), which is also positive definite. Using (1), orthogonality of \(W\), and \((W^{\prime}G_cW)^{-1}=W^{\prime}G_c^{-1}W\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
U(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c})^{-1}U_{S_c}^{\prime}\nu_c
&=\Gamma W(W^{\prime}G_cW)^{-1}W^{\prime}G_cm_c\\
&=\Gamma WW^{\prime}G_c^{-1}WW^{\prime}G_cm_c\\
&=\Gamma m_c.
\end{aligned}
\tag{9}
\]
The right side is the causal cohort mean, rather than an observed-law definition of it: indeed, \(\texttt{ass:rank-two-factor-law}\) and \(\texttt{ass:error-mean}\) imply
\[
\mathbb E_P[Y_i(0)\mid C_i=c]
=\Gamma\mathbb E_P[\lambda_i\mid C_i=c]
 +\mathbb E_P[\varepsilon_i\mid C_i=c]
=\Gamma m_c
=\mu_c(P).
\tag{10}
\]
The left side of (9) is invariant under replacing \(U\) by \(UW_0\) for any orthogonal \(W_0\), as follows either by the same calculation or by cancellation of \(W_0\) and \(W_0^{\prime}\). Since \(P_O\) determines \(\mathcal K(P)\) and \(\nu_c\), (9) is exactly the map in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-functional}\), and it is determined by the entire observed law. Therefore, if \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\) have \((P_0)_O=(P_1)_O\), the map has the same value under both laws and, by (9)--(10), \(\mu(P_0)=\mu(P_1)\). This proves identification of every cohort-time coordinate when the certificate passes.

It remains to prove that the algebraic conclusion after certificate failure cannot, under the frozen primitives alone, be strengthened to causal-target nonidentification. Consider the allowed fixed specification \(T=4\), \(C=1\), and \(S_1=\{1,2,3\}\). Its anchor hypergraph has one edge, so
\[
r_{1,2}(H_3)=1<T-2=2.
\tag{11}
\]
Let
\[
G_0=
\begin{pmatrix}
1&0\\
0&1\\
1&1\\
1&2
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Gamma_0=G_0(G_0^{\prime}G_0)^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Because \(G_0^{\prime}G_0\) is positive definite, \(\Gamma_0^{\prime}\Gamma_0=I_2\). The three two-by-two minors made from rows \(1,2,3\) of \(G_0\) are \(1\), \(1\), and \(-1\); right multiplication by the invertible matrix \((G_0^{\prime}G_0)^{-1/2}\) multiplies each by its nonzero determinant. Hence \(\Gamma_{0,S_1}\) has rank two and lies off the determinantal exceptional set for this single anchor triple, as required by \(\texttt{ass:generic-factor-rows}\).

Fix \(v>0\), take \(p_1=1\), set \(v_{\star}=v^{\star}=v\), and, conditional on the sole cohort, let \(\lambda_i\) be uniform on the circle of radius \(\sqrt{2v}\) in \(\mathbb R^2\). Set \(\varepsilon_i=0\) almost surely. Then
\[
\mathbb E[\lambda_i]=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(\lambda_i)=vI_2,
\qquad
\mathbb E\|\lambda_i\|^{4+\delta}=(2v)^{(4+\delta)/2}.
\tag{13}
\]
Choose
\[
M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{(4+\delta)/2},
\qquad
0<g_{\star}<\lambda_2\!\left(Gamma_{0,S_1}vI_2\Gamma_{0,S_1}^{\prime}\right),
\qquad
0<p_{\star}<1.
\tag{14}
\]
The eigenvalue on the right of (14) is positive because \(\Gamma_{0,S_1}\) has rank two. Equations (12)--(14) verify normalization, exact rank two, the covariance bounds, the local signal gap, the conditional moment radius, mean-zero errors, loading--error orthogonality, and conditional homoskedasticity with \(\sigma_1=0\). Taking independent copies verifies \(\texttt{ass:iid-units}\), while \(p_1=1\) verifies \(\texttt{ass:positive-shares}\). Thus this certificate-failing frozen-model specification is nonempty.

For these primitive radii, \(q_0=4+\delta\), \(v_{\star}=v^{\star}=v\), and \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{q_0/2}\). The already-established \(\texttt{lem:tight-moment-radius-forces-zero-means}\) therefore applies to every \(P\) in this fixed specification and gives
\[
m_c=0,
\qquad
\varepsilon_i=0\ \text{ almost surely given }C_i=c,
\qquad
\mu(P)=0.
\tag{15}
\]
Thus the causal target on this nonempty certificate-failing class is the constant observed-law functional zero. At the same time, (8) gives generic nonuniqueness of its factor plane. Hence failure of the pebble certificate alone entails factor-plane ambiguity, but it does not entail two observed-law-equivalent members with distinct causal means. This establishes the final assertion and completes the proof.

For each \(N\), write
\[
 R_N=
 \inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
 \mathbb E_P L\{\widetilde\mu,\mu(P)\}.
\]
The loss is nonnegative.  Consequently \(R_N\geq0\), while \(\operatorname{thm:minimax-frontier}\) gives
\[
 0\leq R_N
 \leq C_0\min\!\left\{1,\frac{1}{Ns_N^2}\right\}.
\tag{3}
\]
If \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\), the right-hand side of \((3)\) tends to zero.  The squeeze theorem therefore yields \(R_N\to0\), proving sufficiency.

It remains to prove the asserted failure of necessity.  Invoke \(\operatorname{thm:four-mask-early-kill-negative}\).  It supplies an allowed choice of fixed primitive radii and a legal equal-share four-mask family \((P_\eta)\) in the corresponding ambient model, together with constants \(a,b,\eta_0>0\), such that
\[
 a|\eta|\leq s(P_\eta)\leq b|\eta|
 \qquad\text{whenever }0<|\eta|\leq\eta_0,
\tag{4}
\]
and such that \(\mu(P)=0\) for every law \(P\) in that ambient model.  For \(N\geq1\), define
\[
 \eta_N=\frac{\eta_0}{N+1},
 \qquad
 s_N=s(P_{\eta_N}).
\tag{5}
\]
Equation \((4)\) implies \(s_N>0\).  To verify the required upper bound on \(s_N\), let \(x\in\mathbb R^T\).  By \(\operatorname{def:relation-operator}\), by \(0\preceq Q_c\preceq I_{|S_c|}\), and by \(\sum_{c=1}^C p_c=1\),
\[
 x^{\prime}A(P)x
 =\sum_{c=1}^C p_c\|Q_cJ_cx\|_2^2
 \leq\sum_{c=1}^C p_c\|J_cx\|_2^2
 \leq\sum_{c=1}^C p_c\|x\|_2^2
 =\|x\|_2^2.
\tag{6}
\]
Thus \(0\preceq A(P)\preceq I_T\).  The definition of the relation margin then gives \(s(P)\leq1\), so \((5)\) gives \(s_N\in(0,1]\).  Moreover,
\[
 s_N\leq s(P_{\eta_N})=s_N\leq2s_N,
\]
and hence \(P_{\eta_N}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\); every shell in this sequence is nonempty.  The upper inequality in \((4)\) and \((5)\) yield
\[
 Ns_N^2
 \leq \frac{Nb^2\eta_0^2}{(N+1)^2}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{7}
\]
Finally, \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) is a subset of the same ambient model by \(\operatorname{def:margin-shell}\).  Therefore \(\mu(P)=0\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\).  The identically zero estimator is measurable, and the definition of the normalized squared sup-norm loss gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
 \mathbb E_P L\{0,\mu(P)\}=0.
\tag{8}
\]
Nonnegativity of the loss and \((8)\) imply \(R_N=0\) for every \(N\), whereas \((7)\) shows \(Ns_N^2\to0\).  This is the required allowed counterexample to necessity.

Fix \(N\in\mathbb N\) and \(s_N\in(0,1]\) such that \(\mathcal P_N(s_N)\ne\varnothing\), and fix \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\).  The share condition \(p_c\ge p_\star>0\) in \(\mathrm{ass:positive\text{-}shares}\) ensures that every cohort-conditional moment used below is well defined.  Let
\[
\vartheta_0=\bigl(p,\Gamma,(m_c,H_c,\sigma_c)_{c=1}^C\bigr)
\]
be the primitive parameter induced by \(P\), and put \(q_0=4+\delta\).  Conditional Jensen's inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:moment\text{-}radius}\) give, for every \(c\in[C]\),
\[
\|m_c\|_2
=\|\mathbb E_P(\lambda_i\mid C_i=c)\|_2
\le \left\{\mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)\right\}^{1/q_0}
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{1/q_0}=B.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\mathrm{ass:error\text{-}mean}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}homoskedasticity}\),
\[
\mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c)
=\operatorname{tr}\{\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon_i\mid C_i=c)\}
=T\sigma_c^2.
\]
Lyapunov's inequality and \(\mathrm{ass:moment\text{-}radius}\) therefore imply
\[
(T\sigma_c^2)^{q_0/2}
\le \mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}},
\qquad
0\le\sigma_c\le \frac{B}{\sqrt T}\le B,
\tag{2}
\]
where the last inequality uses \(T\ge3\) from the fixed-dimensional model.  The actual conditional law of \(\lambda_i\) given \(C_i=c\) has mean \(m_c\), covariance \(H_c\), and \(q_0\)-moment at most \(M_{\mathrm{mom}}\), so it witnesses \(m\in\mathfrak M_\lambda(H)\) in \(\mathrm{def:admissible\text{-}loading\text{-}means}\).  Equations (1)--(2), together with \(\mathrm{ass:positive\text{-}shares}\), \(\mathrm{ass:factor\text{-}normalization}\), \(\mathrm{ass:loading\text{-}covariance}\), \(\mathrm{ass:local\text{-}signal\text{-}gap}\), and the bounds \(s_N\le s(P)\le2s_N\) from \(\mathrm{ass:singular\text{-}shell}\), verify every constraint in \(\mathrm{def:primitive\text{-}moment\text{-}class}\).  Hence
\[
\vartheta_0\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N).
\tag{3}
\]

We next show that this primitive parameter reproduces the observed moments rather than defining the causal target to equal an observed-law functional.  By \(\mathrm{ass:rank\text{-}two\text{-}factor\text{-}law}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:error\text{-}mean}\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c\}=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.
\tag{4}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_P(\lambda_i\varepsilon_i'\mid C_i=c)
&=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\lambda_i,\varepsilon_i\mid C_i=c)
  +m_c\mathbb E_P(\varepsilon_i'\mid C_i=c)=0,
\end{aligned}
\]
by \(\mathrm{ass:loading\text{-}error\text{-}orthogonality}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:error\text{-}mean}\), and the transposed cross moment is also zero.  Since \(\mathbb E_P(\lambda_i\lambda_i'\mid C_i=c)=H_c+m_cm_c'\), \(\mathrm{ass:conditional\text{-}homoskedasticity}\) then yields
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)Y_i(0)'J_c'\mid C_i=c\}
=\Gamma_{S_c}(H_c+m_cm_c')\Gamma_{S_c}'+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.
\tag{5}
\]
Multiplying (4)--(5) by \(p_c\) and adjoining the cohort-indicator moment \(p_c\) gives, coordinate by coordinate, precisely the population map in \(\mathrm{def:moment\text{-}inversion}\).  Thus
\[
g(\vartheta_0)=\theta(P).
\tag{6}
\]
On the other hand, the causal mean follows from the factor law and the conditional mean-zero error restriction:
\[
\mathbb E_P\{Y_i(0)\mid C_i=c\}=\Gamma m_c=\mu_c(P).
\tag{7}
\]
Equations (6)--(7) prove the required relationship between the observed moment restriction and the causal target.

Suppose first that \(N\ge2k_\alpha\), and define
\[
E_N=\|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\|_{\mathsf m},
\qquad
\mathcal E_N=\{E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\}.
\]
By (3), (6), and the definition of the profiled distance,
\[
d_N
=\min_{\vartheta\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N)}
  \|g(\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
\le \|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
=E_N.
\tag{8}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N\), equations (6) and (8) imply
\[
\|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
=E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\le d_N+\widehat\rho_N,
\]
so \(\vartheta_0\in\mathcal C_N\).  By (7) and the definition of the coordinatewise enclosing rectangle, \(\mu(P)\in\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\) on \(\mathcal E_N\).  The coverage assertion in \(\mathrm{lem:robust\text{-}moment\text{-}ball}\) therefore gives
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\Pr_P\{\mu(P)\in\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\}
\ge
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\Pr_P(\mathcal E_N)
\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{9}
\]
If \(N<2k_\alpha\), \(\mathrm{def:moment\text{-}inversion}\) instead returns \([-B,B]^{CT}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:factor\text{-}normalization}\), (1), and (7),
\[
|\mu_{ct}(P)|\le\|\Gamma m_c\|_2=\|m_c\|_2\le B,
\]
so the fallback rectangle covers with probability one.  This proves (9) for every \(N\).

We next verify measurability.  Set \(K_N=\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\).  It is a nonempty compact subset of a finite-dimensional Euclidean space: nonemptiness follows from (3), while compactness is part of \(\mathrm{def:primitive\text{-}moment\text{-}class}\) and also follows from its closedness and the displayed primitive bounds.  Let \((\vartheta_\ell)_{\ell\ge1}\) be a deterministic countable dense subset of \(K_N\), and let \(h_j(\vartheta)\) denote target coordinate \(j\) of \((\Gamma m_c)_{c=1}^C\).  Continuity of \(g\) gives
\[
d(x)=\min_{\vartheta\in K_N}\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m},
\qquad
|d(x)-d(y)|\le\|x-y\|_{\mathsf m},
\tag{10}
\]
so \(d\) is continuous.  For \(r>0\), define
\[
u_{j,k}(x,r)
=\sup\left\{h_j(\vartheta_\ell):
\|g(\vartheta_\ell)-x\|_{\mathsf m}<d(x)+r+k^{-1},\ \ell\ge1\right\},
\]
assigning the valid lower bound \(-B\) when an indexed constraint fails.  Each \(u_{j,k}\) is measurable as a countable supremum of measurable functions.  Compactness, continuity of \(g\) and \(h_j\), and density give
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}u_{j,k}(x,r)
=\max_{\substack{\vartheta\in K_N:\\
\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m}\le d(x)+r}}h_j(\vartheta).
\tag{11}
\]
Indeed, a dense approximating sequence for any feasible \(\vartheta\) proves that the left side is at least the right side.  Conversely, choose approximate maximizers in the countable suprema; compactness gives a convergent subsequence, and its limit obeys the weak constraint and has objective value no larger than the right side.  Applying the same argument to \(-h_j\) makes the lower endpoint measurable.  The block medians \(\widehat\theta\) and \(\widehat v\), hence \(\widehat\rho_N>0\), are measurable by \(\mathrm{def:robust\text{-}observed\text{-}moments}\).  Substitution of \((x,r)=(\widehat\theta,\widehat\rho_N)\) in (11) proves measurability of all endpoints when \(N\ge2k_\alpha\); the small-sample box is deterministic.  Therefore \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\) is measurable for every \(N\).

It remains to bound its maximal half-width.  The set \(\mathcal C_N\) is nonempty because a minimizer attaining \(d_N\) belongs to it.  For arbitrary \(\vartheta,\widetilde\vartheta\in\mathcal C_N\), the triangle inequality and (8) give, without conditioning on \(\mathcal E_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}
&\le \|g(\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
 +\|g(\widetilde\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}\\
&\le2(d_N+\widehat\rho_N)\\
&\le2(E_N+\widehat\rho_N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
Both parameters lie in \(\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\).  Applying \(\mathrm{lem:observed\text{-}moment\text{-}inverse\text{-}modulus}\) and enlarging its fixed constant to absorb the factor two yields
\[
\max_{c\in[C]}
\|\Gamma m_c-\widetilde\Gamma\widetilde m_c\|_\infty
\le K\min\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\}.
\tag{13}
\]
For each target coordinate, compactness makes both extrema defining the enclosing rectangle attainable.  Applying (13) to their two attaining parameters and then using the definition of \(W\) gives
\[
W(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})
\le K\min\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\},
\tag{14}
\]
after another harmless enlargement of \(K\).  The function \(x\mapsto\min\{1,x\}\) is increasing and concave on \([0,\infty)\).  Jensen's inequality, followed by the expectation bound in \(\mathrm{lem:robust\text{-}moment\text{-}ball}\), therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})
&\le K\min\left\{1,
\frac{\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P(E_N+\widehat\rho_N)}{s_N}\right\}\\
&\le K\min\left\{1,\frac{K_\alpha}{\sqrt N s_N}\right\}\\
&\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
\]
For \(N<2k_\alpha\), the normalized width of the fallback box is at most one.  Since \(s_N\le1\) and \(N<2k_\alpha\),
\[
\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\ge(2k_\alpha)^{-1/2}.
\]
Thus enlarging \(C_\alpha\), which may depend on the fixed \(\alpha\) and fixed moment dimension \(q\), makes (15) valid in the small-sample case as well.

By (9) and the definition of \(\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\), \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\in\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\).  Evaluating the infimum over honest rectangles at this particular rectangle and applying (15) proves
\[
\inf_{\mathcal I_N\in\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N)
\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}.
\]
Finally, \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\) is deterministic.  It is false for every \(N\ge2k_\alpha\), so the expected contribution of the fallback rectangle is exactly zero for every such \(N\).  Dividing this zero contribution by the positive scale \((\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\) leaves zero for every \(s_N\in(0,1]\); hence the claimed little-\(o\) assertion holds uniformly.
